principles.text: Partner count is a vanity metric; a few top partners drive most revenue, so tier them and prune dormant ones.
Automate discovery and outreach at the top of the funnel so you can spend your time on partner relationships.
Avoid flat CPAs on cheap subscriptions; use rev share or delayed, tiered commissions tied to the billing lifecycle.
Open outreach with a bargaining chip like a fee, free product or co-branded page, never a bare program invite.
Onboard affiliates like product users: a five-email welcome sequence in the first five days, aimed at a first commission.

sampleQA.question: Should my SaaS affiliate program pay a flat CPA?

answer.text: Be careful. At WP Engine a flat $200 CPA got gamed: people bought the $30 plan, cancelled the next month and kept the commission.
Rev share lowers fraud risk; a big upfront CPA invites self-submitted signups until you catch them.
Structure rewards around your lifecycle, for example delaying commissions until a customer's third month.
Pay partner types differently; coupon sites shouldn't earn the same as content creators.

sampleQA.question: How do I run affiliate outreach that gets replies?

answer.text: Build three lists: a 25-partner wish list, keyword lists and competitor-traffic lists.
Send five emails over two weeks; a 20% response rate means you're winning.
Lead with a bargaining chip or exploratory budget; generic 'join our program' emails get deleted.
When an affiliate asks for a call, take it immediately; interest is gone within a day or two.

sampleQA.question: I think an affiliate is committing fraud. What do I do?

answer.text: First rule out tracking misconfiguration, attribution windows and cookie overrides; outright scams are rare.
Investigate any click-to-checkout under five minutes; it signals a stolen last click.
Lock down evidence before contacting or freezing the affiliate.
Aim to manage fraud with daily habits, not eliminate it; tools only help you scale the system.
